claim: Using conventions in the action space of deep reinforcement learning agents improves cross-play performance in cooperative multi-agent environments, enabling agents that were trained separately to achieve acceptable scores when paired together.
falsifier: In a cooperative multi-agent environment, train two agents independently with and without convention-augmented action spaces. Then pair agents from different training runs and measure their joint performance to test whether conventions improve cross-play scores.

conditions: conventions are appended to the primitive-action space
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported system, task (Hanabi), population (Rainbow agents), and cross-play experimental conditions; transfer beyond them is unestablished.

title: Augmentation of the action for cross-play performance
